# CANDIDATE-001: OpenSSH resets its receive sequence number on a stray NEWKEYS under strict KEX

Status: **confirmed conformance observation, informational / low severity**.
Reproduced on OpenSSH 9.2p1 (Debian bookworm) and on Alpine edge `openssh-server-10.6_p2-r0` (`sshd -V`: `OpenSSH_10.6p2`; there is no upstream `V_10_6_P2` tag, the source was verified at `V_10_6_P1` and master).
Independently verified in source by a Codex agent: [CANDIDATE-001-verification.md](CANDIDATE-001-verification.md).
Published on 2026-11-07 by team decision, before contacting the maintainers, because it cannot be triggered by an on-path attacker between honest endpoints.

## Observation

Target: OpenSSH 9.2p1 from Debian bookworm (`targets/openssh`, strict KEX backport), client offers `kex-strict-c-v00@openssh.com`.
After a completed handshake, the client sends SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS outside any key exchange
(pre-auth, after a refused rekey, or post-auth).
The server answers SSH_MSG_UNIMPLEMENTED, keeps the current keys,
and resets its receive sequence number to 0.

Evidence (`scripts/seqnr_experiment.py`, 3 runs each, deterministic):

| Variant | Next packet |
|---|---|
| A: strict KEX, client keeps its sequence number | MAC failure, connection closed |
| B: no strict KEX | accepted |
| C: strict KEX, client resets its own sequence number to 0 | accepted |

Dropbear 2024.85 and AsyncSSH 2.17.0 disconnect on the same stray NEWKEYS.
First noticed by the Codex mapper agent from server debug output while fixing a mapper bug,
then confirmed by Claude with the experiment above.

## Root cause

Upstream `openssh-portable` master, `packet.c`, in the receive path (`ssh_packet_read_poll2`, lines 1860–1863 when read on 2026-11-07):

```c
if (*typep == SSH2_MSG_NEWKEYS && ssh->kex->kex_strict) {
    debug_f("resetting read seqnr %u", state->p_read.seqnr);
    state->p_read.seqnr = 0;
}
```

The reset happens in the packet layer for every received NEWKEYS,
before the dispatcher decides the message is unexpected and answers UNIMPLEMENTED,
so the counter is reset although no new keys are installed.
The send path (lines 1380–1383) has the same shape, but OpenSSH only sends NEWKEYS inside a key exchange.

## Why it matters (assessment, low confidence)

draft-miller-sshm-strict-kex-01 §3.3 / OpenSSH PROTOCOL §1.9: the sequence number is reset after sending or receiving NEWKEYS.
The text does not say whether this applies to a NEWKEYS that is not part of a key exchange.
OpenSSH follows the literal text; the other two treat the message as a protocol error.
We read this as a **specification ambiguity**, not a vulnerability; the verification found no normative violation either way.
Creating a fresh valid encrypted NEWKEYS requires the current directional keys, so it takes the legitimate (but misbehaving) peer;
an on-path attacker between two honest endpoints cannot trigger it.
Once a misbehaving peer has sent it, the receiver's transport state breaks an invariant (verification §4):
with `chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com` (nonce and Poly1305 key derived from the sequence number) the receiver can accept
earlier packets of the same direction and key epoch again, and a peer that also resets its own counter reuses nonces in its sending direction;
AES-GCM is unaffected (independent IV counter); HMAC/UMAC see repeated sequence inputs.
These consequences are source-derived, not demonstrated at runtime (our mapper only speaks AES-128-CTR + HMAC-SHA2-256).
The OpenSSH client shares the packet-layer reset: after authentication it continues like the server, during authentication it terminates.

## Next checks

1. ~~Current upstream OpenSSH~~: same code at V_9_6_P1, V_9_9_P2, V_10_6_P1 and master (introduced in 1edb00c, 2023-12-18); behaviour reproduced on 10.6p2 (Alpine).
2. ~~Read upstream `packet.c`~~: done, see Root cause.
3. Other strict-KEX implementations (Go x/crypto/ssh, libssh, russh, wolfSSH, MINA): does any other reset without new keys?
4. Test with `chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com` once the mapper supports it.
5. Decide with the team whether this is worth a note to the OpenSSH developers and to the draft author.
# CANDIDATE-001 verification

Verified on 2026-11-07 by source inspection and experiments against Docker targets bound to 127.0.0.1.
Verdict: **confirmed** for the server after initial KEX, with important client-state and impact qualifications.
No downloaded source was built or executed.
The only existing repository file read for execution was the authorized experiment; this report is a new file.

## 1. Receive path and key state — confirmed

In [V_10_6_P1 packet.c:1736–1786](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/packet.c#L1736), the packet is authenticated/decrypted using the current receive sequence number, that original number is saved for dispatch, and the counter is incremented.
At packet.c:1849–1852, the test is simply `if (*typep == SSH2_MSG_NEWKEYS && ssh->kex->kex_strict)`, followed by `state->p_read.seqnr = 0;`.
It does not test whether a KEX is active or new keys are pending.
This occurs inside `ssh_packet_read_poll2()` before it returns through the read API to the dispatcher.
In [V_10_6_P1 dispatch.c:87–114](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/dispatch.c#L87), reading precedes `(*ssh->dispatch[type])(type, seqnr, ssh)`.
Thus the reset precedes the decision that NEWKEYS is unexpected.
The UNIMPLEMENTED payload contains the original received sequence number, not the reset value.

In [V_10_6_P1 kex.c:429–437](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/kex.c#L429), `kex_send_newkeys()` resets the transport dispatch table, sends NEWKEYS, then registers `kex_input_newkeys` as the expected receive handler.
At kex.c:562–575, the legitimate receive handler immediately restores NEWKEYS to `kex_protocol_error`, checks the payload end, and calls `ssh_set_newkeys(ssh, MODE_IN)`.
At kex.c:600–603 it marks KEX complete and clears `KEX_INITIAL` and KEX-init flags.
At kex.c:994–1015, strict KEX is selected only during initial KEX by checking the opposite role's strict marker, and remains enabled afterwards.
At kex.c:232–246, `kex_protocol_error()` disconnects for an unexpected message during strict initial KEX, but otherwise constructs `SSH2_MSG_UNIMPLEMENTED` and returns success.

The exact handler outside KEX depends on the application phase, rather than always being `dispatch_protocol_error()`.
[V_10_6_P1 auth2.c:175–179](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/auth2.c#L175) initializes the server authentication dispatcher with `dispatch_protocol_error`.
[V_10_6_P1 serverloop.c:905–922](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/serverloop.c#L905) does the same for the server connection loop and explicitly enables KEXINIT for rekeying.
Both that default handler, at dispatch.c:40–51, and `kex_protocol_error()` send UNIMPLEMENTED.
Neither installs keys.

[V_10_6_P1 packet.c:976–1040](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/packet.c#L976) shows that installing keys requires moving `ssh->kex->newkeys[mode]` into packet state and rebuilding the cipher context via `cipher_init()`.
The stray-message receive branch never calls this routine.
The receive key, cipher context, CTR/CBC state or GCM invocation state, and MAC key stay in use; only the SSH receive sequence counter is reset by this branch.
The opposite direction's send counter is not reset by receiving NEWKEYS, including when sending the UNIMPLEMENTED response.
The send-side reset at packet.c:1376–1382 is adjacent to an unconditional `ssh_set_newkeys(ssh, MODE_OUT)` for an outgoing NEWKEYS, so it must not be described as an equivalent supported way for OpenSSH to send stray NEWKEYS while retaining keys.

## 2. OpenSSH client symmetry — partly

The packet-layer behavior is shared between client and server and the receive reset has no role check.
After authentication, [V_10_6_P1 clientloop.c:2844–2862](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/clientloop.c#L2844) sets the default handler to `dispatch_protocol_error`, enables KEXINIT, and leaves stray NEWKEYS on the default error path.
An established client therefore also resets, sends UNIMPLEMENTED, retains current keys, and continues.
After a subsequent completed KEX, the restored `kex_protocol_error` handler has the same nonfatal outcome.

During user authentication, however, [V_10_6_P1 sshconnect2.c:462–465 and 563–566](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/sshconnect2.c#L462) installs `input_userauth_error` as the default handler, which calls `fatal_f("bad message during authentication: type %d", type)`.
In that phase a stray server NEWKEYS still resets the counter first, but terminates the client instead of sending UNIMPLEMENTED and continuing.
Unexpected initial strict-KEX NEWKEYS also terminates through KEX error handling.
Client conclusions are source-verified, not reproduced with a malicious local server.

## 3. Introduction and versions — confirmed

The introducing portable commit is [1edb00c58f8a6875fad6a497aa2bacf37f9e6cd5](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/commit/1edb00c58f8a6875fad6a497aa2bacf37f9e6cd5), dated 2023-12-18, titled `upstream: implement "strict key exchange" in ssh and sshd`.
Its OpenBSD commit ID is `2a66ac962f0a630d7945fee54004ed9e9c439f14`.
The downloaded patch adds the unconditional strict NEWKEYS receive reset; the introducing packet.c already has it at lines 1693–1696.
The GitHub tags API and packet.c commit-history API supplied tag SHAs, dates, and commit messages.
Individual API lookups for the introduction and rekey-hardening commits returned HTTP 403, so their exact diffs were obtained with curl from GitHub commit patch URLs and checked against raw source.

Later handling did change, but does not fix or prevent this stray-message reset.
[72b05ecd141b9683285dcdb439de01903c1a07d3](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/commit/72b05ecd141b9683285dcdb439de01903c1a07d3), dated 2026-05-31, rejects non-KEX messages after receiving a KEXINIT and tracks `KEX_INIT_RECVD`.
In master packet.c:1968–1976 the new default-case check returns `SSH_ERR_PROTOCOL_ERROR` for such messages.
NEWKEYS passes `ssh_packet_type_is_kex()` at master packet.c:1396–1404, and a bare NEWKEYS outside KEX does not have the active-KEX prerequisite anyway.
This hardening therefore does not imply that unexpected NEWKEYS disconnects.
[f7a2c31dbfc10c2d1111830f6756ff9b3a1318dd](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/commit/f7a2c31dbfc10c2d1111830f6756ff9b3a1318dd), dated 2026-10-30, changes strict-KEX failures from process-fatal handling to returned errors with poisoned packet state; master kex.c:237 still limits this strict unexpected-message failure to `KEX_INITIAL`.

## 4. Protocol impact — partly; misbehaving peer required

A party creating a fresh valid encrypted NEWKEYS after initial KEX needs the relevant directional encryption and authentication keys, barring cryptographic compromise or forgery.
This can be the legitimate remote endpoint and does not require successful SSH user authentication.
A passive observer or ordinary on-path attacker cannot choose or modify an authenticated packet's type to trigger this reset.
An attacker can retransmit ciphertext, so “only key holders can send one” needs the qualification that creation of a fresh valid packet differs from replay.
With two honest endpoints, old NEWKEYS packets do not provide this trigger: initial NEWKEYS was under the initial unencrypted transport, and rekey NEWKEYS was protected with the preceding keys, which the receiver replaces upon legitimate processing.
The finding supplies no way for an on-path attacker to get a valid stray NEWKEYS under the receiver's current keys and sequence state between honest endpoints.

For `chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com`, [V_10_6_P1 cipher-chachapoly.c:77–110 and 125–134](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/cipher-chachapoly.c#L77) derives the nonce and per-packet Poly1305 key from `POKE_U64(seqbuf, seqnr)`.
After a misbehaving peer supplies the stray message, the honest receiver reuses old receive-side key/nonce combinations when processing sequence numbers starting again at zero.
Previously recorded packets from that same direction and current key epoch can then authenticate and decrypt again at matching sequence numbers, subject to application-state validation and intervening rekeying or closure.
A peer which also resets its sending counter and encrypts new packets under the retained key causes actual encryption nonce and Poly1305-key reuse in its own sending direction.
The honest receiver's reset does not make its independent outgoing direction reuse nonces.
These are source-derived consequences, not a demonstrated attack between honest peers or a runtime ChaCha replay test.

For AES-GCM, [V_10_6_P1 cipher.c:343–375](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/cipher.c#L343) uses an independent cipher-context invocation IV (`EVP_CTRL_GCM_IV_GEN`), not the SSH sequence number as its nonce.
Keeping that context while resetting the SSH counter does not reset the GCM IV, does not cause GCM nonce reuse, and does not by itself allow old ciphertext to authenticate again.
The GCM path does not use a separate SSH MAC with the reset sequence number.

For HMAC and UMAC modes, [V_10_6_P1 mac.c:158–188](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_10_6_P1/mac.c#L158) uses the sequence number as an HMAC input prefix or UMAC nonce.
Packet.c:1736–1761 supplies it both for EtM authentication over ciphertext and conventional MAC authentication over plaintext.
Resetting therefore repeats MAC sequence inputs, and repeats UMAC nonces, but does not rewind CTR counters or CBC chaining state.
HMAC input-prefix reuse alone is not an HMAC break.
With conventional MACs and CTR/CBC, replayed ciphertext ordinarily decrypts differently and fails authentication; with CTR plus EtM, an old ciphertext tag can match the reset counter but cipher-stream desynchronization prevents reliable replay of the original plaintext packet.
CBC plus EtM also authenticates the old ciphertext at a reused sequence number, while its first plaintext block changes with the current chaining value, so packet parsing and application acceptance require separate analysis and must not be claimed generically.
No CBC/EtM or UMAC forgery or application replay was demonstrated here.
There is no honest-client/honest-server scenario established by this finding that reuses an encryption key/nonce pair or accepts a replay.
All identified new effects require a misbehaving or compromised endpoint first producing a valid stray NEWKEYS.

## 5. Specification and other implementations — confirmed with interpretation caveat

[Draft-miller-sshm-strict-kex-01 §3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-miller-sshm-strict-kex-01#section-3.3) places resets at KEX completion, but its operational receive instruction says the counter “MUST be reset after a SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS is received.”
That literal receive instruction matches OpenSSH's reset even for an unexpected packet, while the section's KEX-completion framing leaves treatment of stray NEWKEYS unclear.
[V_9_6_P1 PROTOCOL:161–164](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/V_9_6_P1/PROTOCOL#L161) explicitly requires reset after sending or receiving NEWKEYS and says the behavior persists for the connection.
OpenSSH follows that literal rule.
Neither text explicitly requires continuing after an out-of-KEX NEWKEYS, so literal reset compliance does not prove that continuing is the intended specification behavior.
Calling this a specification ambiguity is reasonable editorial interpretation, not proof of a normative violation or proof that no security consequence can exist.

[Dropbear DROPBEAR_2024.85 src/common-kex.c:124–128](https://github.com/mkj/dropbear/blob/DROPBEAR_2024.85/src/common-kex.c#L124) checks `!(ses.kexstate.sentkexinit && ses.kexstate.recvkexinit)` in `switch_keys()` and calls `dropbear_exit("Unexpected newkeys message")`.
Its `recv_msg_newkeys()` at lines 194–205 calls `switch_keys()` before the strict-mode `ses.recvseq = 0`, so a bare stray NEWKEYS outside KEX exits before that reset.
At lines 151–160, completed exchanges call `kexinitialise()`; lines 241–243 clear the exchange state.
This confirms termination rather than continued operation with an unchanged key and reset counter.

[AsyncSSH v2.17.0 asyncssh/connection.py:2328–2344](https://github.com/ronf/asyncssh/blob/v2.17.0/asyncssh/connection.py#L2328) accepts NEWKEYS only if `_next_recv_encryption` exists, consumes that pending encryption state, and otherwise raises `ProtocolError('New keys not negotiated')`.
Packet processing calls that handler at lines 1596–1599, before the receive-sequence reset at lines 1623–1626.
The receive error path at lines 1335–1337 sends a disconnect and force-closes the connection.
Thus a stray message fails before the receive reset and the connection does not continue.
These other-implementation verdicts are from tagged source; the present verification did not rerun their containers.

## 6. Local experiments — confirmed

`uv run python scripts/seqnr_experiment.py openssh openssh-alpine-edge` completed successfully.
For each target and each prefix (pre-auth refused rekey, pre-auth bare NEWKEYS, post-auth bare NEWKEYS), all three repetitions were deterministic.
Every stray NEWKEYS returned UNIMPLEMENTED.
Variant A (strict, sender counter retained) then returned CLOSED; variant B (non-strict) and variant C (strict, sender counter reset) accepted the authentication or channel-open probe.
The abstraction reports CLOSED here, not an explicit MAC-error message; source analysis establishes the sequence-dependent authentication explanation.
The mapper uses AES-128-CTR with HMAC-SHA2-256, so these results establish counter reset and continuing cipher state, not ChaCha or GCM behavior experimentally.

A second inline experiment used `smlearn.testbed` and `SSHMapper`, with both targets, before and after authentication.
It sent a stray NEWKEYS, reset only the mapper's outgoing sequence to zero, sent IGNORE, then repeated that pair and sent the final authentication/channel-open probe.
All four runs produced `UNIMPLEMENTED, NO_RESP, UNIMPLEMENTED, NO_RESP` followed by `UA_SUCCESS+GLOBAL_REQUEST` before authentication or `CH_OPEN_SUCCESS` after authentication.
This confirms that a second stray NEWKEYS resets again while cipher state continues.
Observed banners were `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u10` and `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_10.6`.
The edge target's metadata says 10.6p2, but its banner does not establish that portable patchlevel, and upstream's latest tag is V_10_6_P1.
No remote SSH target was contacted.

## Corrections and final assessment

The original server observation and reset-before-dispatch root cause are correct.
Its conditional statement that a client which also resets can reuse ChaCha nonces is correct, but should explicitly identify that client as a misbehaving sender; the honest receiver does not thereby encrypt with repeated nonces.
A blanket “no replay” claim would also be wrong once a malicious peer has supplied the trigger; the original does not demonstrate that conditional ChaCha behavior.
Client symmetry needs the user-authentication termination exception.
The original's “current upstream 10.6p2” statement is not supported by the tag API or observed banner and should not be published as a verified upstream version.
The status text simultaneously says candidate/maintainers not contacted and “Published”; this verification establishes technical behavior only, not publication or disclosure status.

Severity: **informational / low**, with **high confidence** in the server state transition and source-level client qualification, and **moderate confidence** in the overall severity assessment.
The finding demonstrates permissive handling and a cryptographic state invariant violation induced by a misbehaving peer, including conditional ChaCha replay acceptance at the transport layer.
It does not demonstrate authentication bypass, disclosure of an honest peer's outgoing plaintext, privilege escalation, or an on-path attack between honest endpoints.
Publish as a qualified conformance/specification observation rather than an established remotely exploitable vulnerability.
"""Does a server reset its receive sequence number on a NEWKEYS that is not part of a key exchange?

Variants after a completed handshake, for each target:
  A  strict KEX on,  client keeps its sequence number after the stray NEWKEYS
  B  strict KEX off, client keeps its sequence number
  C  strict KEX on,  client resets its own outgoing sequence number to 0 after the stray NEWKEYS
If A fails, B succeeds and C succeeds, the server reset its receive counter without new keys.
"""
from smlearn import testbed
from smlearn.ssh.mapper import SSHMapper

WORDS = {
    "pre-auth refused rekey": (["KEXINIT", "KEX30", "NEWKEYS", "SR_AUTH", "KEXINIT", "KEX30", "NEWKEYS"], "UA_PW_OK"),
    "pre-auth bare NEWKEYS": (["KEXINIT", "KEX30", "NEWKEYS", "SR_AUTH", "NEWKEYS"], "UA_PW_OK"),
    "post-auth bare NEWKEYS": (["KEXINIT", "KEX30", "NEWKEYS", "SR_AUTH", "UA_PW_OK", "NEWKEYS"], "CH_OPEN"),
}

import sys
for name in (sys.argv[1:] or ["openssh", "dropbear", "asyncssh"]):
    inst = testbed.start(testbed.load_target(name))
    try:
        for label, (prefix, probe) in WORDS.items():
            row = []
            for variant, strict, reset in (("A", True, False), ("B", False, False), ("C", True, True)):
                m = SSHMapper(inst.host, inst.port, timeout=0.4, quiet=0.1, strict_kex=strict)
                outs = set()
                for _ in range(3):
                    m.reset()
                    pre = [m.step(i) for i in prefix]
                    if reset:
                        m.outgoing.sequence = 0
                    outs.add((pre[-1], m.step(probe)))
                m.close()
                (last, probe_out), = outs if len(outs) == 1 else [("NONDET", str(outs))]
                row.append(f"{variant}: NEWKEYS->{last}, {probe}->{probe_out}")
            print(f"{name:9} {label:24} | " + " | ".join(row))

# libssh server target

Uses the C server API from the official libssh 0.12.2 release:
https://www.libssh.org/files/0.12/libssh-0.12.2.tar.xz
The Dockerfile verifies the release archive's SHA-256 checksum and builds a
stripped shared library in a separate build stage. The runtime contains only
the server, libssh, OpenSSL and the Debian base dependencies.

The server generates an Ed25519 host key at startup, listens on container port
22, and uses libssh's default algorithm lists (including curve25519-sha256,
aes128-ctr, hmac-sha2-256 and strict KEX). Compression is disabled at build time,
so it offers none. No system SSH configuration is loaded.

Only password authentication for test/test succeeds. Each connection has its
own thread and accepts session channels after authentication. An exec request
for any command succeeds and returns exit status 0, EOF and channel close;
the command is not executed. Incoming channel data is consumed and discarded.
Transport parsing, key exchange, rekey, authentication message handling and
channel framing are provided by libssh without protocol patches.

initial strict_kex_active: True

NEWKEYS => NO_RESP strict= True

NEWKEYS => NO_RESP strict= False
CH_OPEN => NO_RESP strict= False

The initial server KEXINIT includes `kex-strict-s-v00@openssh.com`;
the authenticated rekey KEXINIT omits it. Both offer curve25519-sha256.
The mapper sets strict_kex_active to False on receipt of the second KEXINIT.
libssh retains strict KEX and resets packet sequence numbers on NEWKEYS.
This gives incompatible sequence numbers for the following encrypted traffic.
The test fails at the final CH_OPEN_SUCCESS assertion (actual: NO_RESP),
after both key exchanges have returned KEX31+NEWKEYS.

[0.12.2 source archive](https://www.libssh.org/files/0.12/libssh-0.12.2.tar.xz):

- `src/kex.c:557–565`: enables the persistent SSH_SESSION_FLAG_KEX_STRICT
  when the client offers strict KEX.
- `src/packet.c:2100–2102`: resets send_seq on NEWKEYS in strict KEX.
- `src/packet_cb.c:164–166`: resets recv_seq on NEWKEYS in strict KEX.

The unchanged mapper's SSHMapper._received assigns strict_kex_active from
whether each received KEXINIT contains the server marker, and _install uses
that value to decide whether to reset sequence numbers. The mismatch is
therefore an interoperability finding, not a missing cipher or a target
configuration error. No workaround was applied; work stopped as requested.

changes and workarounds for implementation behavior differences.

"""Start and stop target implementations as local Docker containers.

Every container publishes its port on 127.0.0.1 only, on a random host port,
so many instances of the same target can run side by side.
"""

import json
import socket
import subprocess
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

TARGETS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "targets"


@dataclass
class Target:
    name: str
    implementation: str
    source: str
    port: int
    user: str = "test"
    password: str = "test"

    @property
    def image(self) -> str:
        return f"smlearn-{self.name}"


def load_target(name: str) -> Target:
    data = json.loads((TARGETS_DIR / name / "target.json").read_text())
    return Target(**{k: data[k] for k in Target.__dataclass_fields__ if k in data})


def list_targets() -> list[str]:
    return sorted(p.parent.name for p in TARGETS_DIR.glob("*/target.json"))


def build(target: Target) -> None:
    subprocess.run(["docker", "build", "-q", "-t", target.image, str(TARGETS_DIR / target.name)],
                   check=True, capture_output=True)


@dataclass
class Instance:
    target: Target
    container_id: str
    host: str
    port: int

    def stop(self) -> None:
        subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", self.container_id], capture_output=True)

    def logs(self) -> str:
        r = subprocess.run(["docker", "logs", self.container_id], capture_output=True, text=True)
        return r.stdout + r.stderr


def start(target: Target, ready_timeout: float = 30.0) -> Instance:
    """Run one container and wait until it sends an SSH identification line."""
    cid = subprocess.run(
        ["docker", "run", "-d", "--rm", "--label", "smlearn=1",
         "-p", f"127.0.0.1::{target.port}", target.image],
        check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    out = subprocess.run(["docker", "port", cid, f"{target.port}/tcp"],
                         check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    host_port = int(out.splitlines()[0].rsplit(":", 1)[1])
    inst = Instance(target, cid, "127.0.0.1", host_port)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + ready_timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            with socket.create_connection((inst.host, inst.port), timeout=2) as s:
                if s.recv(256).startswith(b"SSH-"):
                    return inst
        except OSError:
            pass
        time.sleep(0.3)
    logs = inst.logs()
    inst.stop()
    raise RuntimeError(f"{target.name} did not become ready:\n{logs}")

                        outputs.append(name)
                    deadline = time.monotonic() + self.quiet
                    continue
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    break
                self.sock.settimeout(remaining)
                data = self.sock.recv(65536)
                if not data:
                    self.close()
                    outputs.append('CLOSED')
                    break
                self.buffer.extend(data)
            except socket.timeout:
                break
            except OSError:
                self.close()
                outputs.append('CLOSED')
            except ValueError:
                self.close()
                outputs.append('BAD_PACKET')

    def _payload(self, symbol):
        if symbol == 'KEXINIT':
            kex = 'curve25519-sha256,curve25519-sha256@libssh.org'
            if self.strict_kex:
                kex += ',kex-strict-c-v00@openssh.com'
            lists = (kex, 'ssh-ed25519,rsa-sha2-256,ecdsa-sha2-nistp256',
                     'aes128-ctr', 'aes128-ctr', 'hmac-sha2-256', 'hmac-sha2-256',
                     'none', 'none', '', '')
            self.client_kex = b'\x14' + bytes(16) + b''.join(string(x) for x in lists) + b'\0' + uint32(0)
            return self.client_kex
        if symbol == 'KEX30':
            self.private_key = X25519PrivateKey.generate()
            return b'\x1e' + string(self.private_key.public_key().public_bytes_raw())
        if symbol == 'NEWKEYS':
            return b'\x15'
        if symbol in ('SR_AUTH', 'SR_CONN'):
            return b'\x05' + string('ssh-userauth' if symbol == 'SR_AUTH' else 'ssh-connection')

            payload = b'\x32' + string(self.user) + string('ssh-connection')
            if symbol == 'UA_NONE':
                return payload + string('none')
            password = self.password if symbol == 'UA_PW_OK' else self.password + '-wrong'
            return payload + string('password') + b'\0' + string(password)
        if symbol == 'CH_OPEN':
            return b'\x5a' + string('session') + uint32(0) + uint32(2**21) + uint32(32768)
        if symbol.startswith('CH_'):
            channel = uint32(self.channel)
            return {
                'CH_CLOSE': b'\x61' + channel,
                'CH_EOF': b'\x60' + channel,
                'CH_DATA': b'\x5e' + channel + string(b'x'),
                'CH_REQUEST_EXEC': b'\x62' + channel + string('exec') + b'\x01' + string('true'),
            }[symbol]
        return {'IGNORE': b'\x02' + string(b''),
                'DEBUG': b'\x04\0' + string(b'') + string(b''),
                'UNIMPLEMENTED': b'\x03' + uint32(0),
                'DISCONNECT': b'\x01' + uint32(11) + string(b'') + string(b'')}[symbol]

    def step(self, symbol):
        if symbol not in INPUTS:
            raise ValueError(f'unknown SSH input: {symbol}')
        if self.sock is None:
            return 'NO_CONN'
        if symbol in ('CH_CLOSE', 'CH_EOF', 'CH_DATA', 'CH_REQUEST_EXEC') and self.channel is None:
            return 'NO_CHANNEL'
        payload = self._payload(symbol)
        try:
            self.sock.sendall(self.outgoing.encode(payload))
        except OSError:
            self.close()
            return 'CLOSED'
        self.trace.append(('>', NAMES.get(payload[0], f'MSG{payload[0]}'), payload.hex()))
        if symbol == 'NEWKEYS':
            self._install(self.outgoing, True)
        elif symbol == 'CH_CLOSE':
            self.channel = None
        return self._collect(self.timeout)

# CANDIDATE-002: libssh leaves a stray-NEWKEYS session in an error state with an open socket

Status: confirmed local conformance observation; provisional informational / low severity.
Investigated on 2026-11-07 against existing Docker targets published only on 127.0.0.1.
Downloaded source was inspected only, never built or executed.

## Observation

After initial key exchange, a stray SSH_MSG_NEWKEYS makes libssh 0.12.2 stop processing that connection.
It neither replies nor immediately closes TCP.
Correct password authentication subsequently produces no reply, regardless of strict KEX or a client sequence reset.
This is a terminal session error left open by the target application's event loop, not installation of empty keys, a key exchange waiting for completion, or evidence of a whole-server hang.

The original "'`results/seqnr/*.txt` cover twelve implementations/configurations.
For bare NEWKEYS, libssh is silent in all variants; russh continues with the original transport state; OpenSSH continues with a strict-mode receive-counter reset; the remaining targets close.
The “pre-auth refused rekey” row must be interpreted separately: the preceding inputs can constitute a real rekey or fail earlier, so its final NEWKEYS is not uniformly a stray message across implementations.
The bare pre-auth and post-auth rows isolate this observation.

## Local experiments and exact outputs

Reproduction command: `uv run python scripts/stray_newkeys_followup.py`.
The new script uses the unchanged mapper and testbed, AES-128-CTR / HMAC-SHA2-256, and only the existing libssh Docker image.
Each NEWKEYS and immediate authentication/channel probe waits five seconds.
Variants A/B/C mean strict with retained counter, non-strict with retained counter, and strict with outgoing counter reset respectively.
Four affected sessions remain open together while a fifth connection completes authentication and opens a channel.
Raw output is preserved in [libssh-followup.txt](../results/seqnr/libssh-followup.txt).

`NO_RESP` means the collection deadline expired without an SSH response or TCP EOF; it is not a claim that the server thread was blocked inside a cipher routine.
The idle watch is bounded and cannot establish that a connection never closes.
The process counters below measure this existing thread-per-connection target, not every possible application embedding libssh.

## Tagged source and root cause

Source archives are stored under the requested scratch directory `codex-libssh-russh-src`.
The GitHub tag `libssh-0.12.2` resolves through annotated tag object `2d3aa9b36ab543049ca002c5b85c310ac328469b` to commit `07430deb9b97b751ec5ea5a7fc307f40bf042e0a`.
The russh `v0.65.1` tag resolves to `b33092aad1e51c66258a12e8b83fc473a68d9d34`.
SHA-256 of the downloaded codeload archives:

```text
92fef8a348070a6786667ed724d5e808d2530464bac37559a8d59c70ab1f1a83  libssh.tar.gz
fedda194924e6ec1c24f3247dfe8aab2c88c26db3e54a961318e9987297de655  russh.tar.gz
```

All libssh file:line references below refer to that tag.
[packet.c:68](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L68) registers `ssh_packet_newkeys` in the default callback table.
However, [packet.c:326–351](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L326) first filters NEWKEYS:

```c
if (session->session_state != SSH_SESSION_STATE_DH) {
    rc = SSH_PACKET_DENIED;
    break;
}
```

It additionally requires `dh_handshake_state == DH_STATE_NEWKEYS_SENT`.
After initial KEX, the bare message fails the session-state requirement.
[packet.c:1575–1588](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L1575) executes callbacks only for allowed packets.
The denied branch records `Packet filter: rejected packet (type %d)` with `SSH_FATAL` and jumps to `error`.
[packet.c:1626–1629](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L1626) then does:

```c
session->session_state = SSH_SESSION_STATE_ERROR;
SSH_LOG(SSH_LOG_PACKET, "Packet: processed %zu bytes", processed);
return processed;
```

This branch does not send DISCONNECT, close the socket, or clear `alive`.
On subsequent input, [packet.c:1309–1311](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L1309) tests the error state and jumps straight to the same error return, before packet decryption.
The socket callback at [socket.c:377–385](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/socket.c#L377) consumes only the returned byte count and stops retrying when that count is zero.
This explains silence without an immediate busy loop; further incoming bytes may remain buffered instead of being processed.
No memory-growth stress experiment was performed.

Even if reached directly, [packet_cb.c:155–162](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet_cb.c#L155) repeats the same session/DH checks and errors before the strict receive-counter reset at lines 164–166.
Its error path at lines 290–299 also sets the session error state.
Thus this observation is not the OpenSSH reset-before-dispatch behavior from CANDIDATE-001.

Neither filter failure nor callback state-check failure touches `next_crypto` or `current_crypto`.
The real key-switch routine, [packet.c:2165–2220](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/packet.c#L2165), marks directional use of `next_crypto`, retires current directional use, and promotes `next_crypto` only once both directions have switched.
It then allocates a fresh pending crypto object and copies the session ID into it.
That pending object existing after KEX does not mean it becomes active on a stray NEWKEYS: this error path never calls `ssh_packet_set_newkeys()`.
The existing current crypto remains installed, but the session error gate prevents using it for later packets.
The accepted stray packet itself increments the receive counter in the normal packet path at packet.c:1538; no strict reset occurs.

## Per-connection versus whole-server impact

`targets/libssh/server.c` creates a detached thread per accepted connection.
After `ssh_handle_key_exchange()`, its thread loops on `ssh_is_connected(s)` and calls `ssh_event_dopoll(event, 1000)`, breaking only on `SSH_ERROR`.
[session.c:712–718](https://github.com/libssh/libssh-mirror/blob/libssh-0.12.2/src/session.c#L712) implements connection status as `return session->alive;`, without checking `session_state`.
